## Excursions to the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands: which one should you choose?

The [Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) are often combined on a journey along Peru's Pacific coast, although the experiences are completely different. The Nazca geoglyphs are viewed from the air or designated ground viewpoints, while visitors take a boat to the rocky Ballestas Islands to observe birds and marine wildlife.

The practical difficulty is that the two attractions are separated by considerable distances and different transport stages. We offer a scenic flight, combined trips from Lima and options with an overnight stay or private transport. **They do not all include the same activities:** in some itineraries, flying over the geoglyphs is an optional extra.

## A flight above the Nazca Lines

The separate [Nazca Lines Scenic Flight excursion](/peru/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/nazca-lines-flight/) focuses on geoglyphs created by ancient desert cultures. Our excursion includes a **35-minute flight in a small aircraft**. From above, passengers can see animal and bird figures, geometric shapes and long lines.

UNESCO lists the Nazca and Palpa Lines and Geoglyphs as World Heritage. The site covers a vast area of desert where the designs were made by removing the dark surface stones to reveal lighter ground below. The large compositions are easier to appreciate from the air than on an ordinary walk at ground level.

The flight's duration is not the duration of an entire trip from Lima. Travelers also need to reach the airfield, wait for departure and make the return journey. In unfavorable weather, the flight may be rescheduled or changed under the operator's rules.

## Ballestas: a boat excursion to see marine wildlife

The Ballestas Islands lie off the [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/) Peninsula and are known for large colonies of seabirds and sea lions. Along the way, boats often pass the **Paracas Candelabra**, an enormous figure on a coastal slope. It should not be confused with the Nazca Lines: it is in a different location and is seen during the marine part of the trip.

During the boat excursion, Humboldt penguins and other coastal wildlife may also appear. Wild animals move freely, so sightings vary with the season and weather. The standard nature excursion does not include landing on the islands; visitors observe them from the boat in accordance with conservation restrictions.

Wind and swell matter on the sea excursion. If you are prone to seasickness, consider this when choosing the time and duration of the trip. Weather, permits and sea conditions may affect the order of stops.

## Combining Nazca and Ballestas in one or two days

On a trip from [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), the main question is how much time to allocate to the road. Paracas is closer to the capital, while the Nazca geoglyphs are considerably farther south. Combining two memorable attractions can therefore involve a long travel day.

For **one day**, only a specially planned combined itinerary with an early start and confirmed boat and flight segments is suitable. A standalone 35-minute scenic flight does not automatically include a Ballestas visit in the remaining time.

With **two days**, you can spend a night on the coast, distribute travel time more comfortably and decide whether to book a separate flight. Distinguish an included visit to Paracas from an optional aviation activity: it affects scheduling, price and bad-weather decisions.

## Safety on flights and wildlife outings

On a sightseeing flight in a small aircraft, the pilot changes direction to give passengers views of different geoglyphs. Travelers susceptible to motion sickness should ask the operator about precautions and restrictions beforehand. The actual duration, departure airfield and sequence of viewing must match the ticket and confirmed program.

During the boat trip, remain seated when instructed by the crew, follow safety rules and do not attempt to approach wild animals independently. Protected marine areas have specific visitor regulations. No one can promise that every bird or animal will be visible in all weather.

Programs along the [Peruvian coast](/peru/) combine archaeology and marine nature, but it is better to compare the actual sequence of activities than just a list of attractions when choosing the right excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about Nazca and Ballestas excursions

### Are the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands in the same place?

No. The lines are in the Nazca Desert, while the Ballestas Islands are near Paracas. A separate transfer or carefully planned air connection is needed between the aerial and marine experiences.

### Does the two-day itinerary include a flight over Nazca?

On our [two-day program](/peru/paracas/paracas-nazca-two-days/), the flight is listed as an optional extra. Its inclusion must be confirmed separately before booking.

### Can visitors land on the Ballestas Islands?

The standard boat excursion is conducted from the water, without tourist landings on the islands. This helps protect habitats of marine animals and birds.

### Which option suits a very limited schedule?

First decide whether the geoglyphs or the wildlife matter more to you. If you want both experiences in a single day, there is a [combined itinerary](/peru/paracas/peru-paracas-nazca-full-day/), but it requires an early departure and several transport stages.
